## Appearance

Marilla is a tall, thin, and gaunt woman with sharp angles and no curves. Her dark hair, which shows gray streaks, is worn twisted behind her in a hard little knot fastened with two wire hairpins. Though described as a dark and homely child in her youth, her appearance over time has aged to look old, worn, and tired, albeit with a much softer face.

## Personality

A sober, middle-aged woman, she is known for her sensible, self-contained demeanor and rigid conscience. Characterized as strict, stern, and repressed, she generally views life through prose, detests cats, and rarely permits herself to display excitement or deep emotion. Despite her unsympathetic and critical tendencies, she is deeply determined and occasionally yields to subtle affection or sarcasm following a moment of self-betrayal. She has felt a duty to drill [Anne](../character/anne.md) into a tranquil uniformity of disposition, though she also worries over her and suffers from frequent headaches. Celebrated in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) for making three-year-old homemade currant wine, she is also skilled at crafting round braided mats. Her quiet hopes were realized when she experienced profound happiness upon learning that [Anne](../character/anne.md) was going to marry [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md).

## History

Marilla Cuthbert and her brother [Matthew](../character/matthew.md) decided to adopt an orphan boy from [Nova Scotia](../codex/places.md#nova-scotia) to help with farm work at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables), but a mix-up resulted in a young girl named [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) arriving instead. Although initially shocked and intent on returning her, Marilla grew pity for Anne's past, agreed to let her stay, and took on the task of raising and educating her. Despite early friction over Anne's dramatic behavior—including an incident where [Anne](../character/anne.md) accidentally gave currant wine to a friend and another where Marilla wrongly accused [Anne](../character/anne.md) of losing her inherited amethyst brooch—Marilla developed a deep affection for the child. When [Matthew](../character/matthew.md) suddenly passed away and Marilla faced losing her failing eyesight, she considered selling [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables), but [Anne](../character/anne.md) gave up her college scholarship to stay home and teach locally. Marilla later agreed to take in her dying cousin's orphaned twins, [Davy](../character/davy-keith.md) and [Dora](../character/dora.md) Keith, and took on her long-time neighbor [Rachel Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) as a housemate so [Anne](../character/anne.md) could attend [Redmond College](../codex/places.md#redmond-college). She hosted Anne's wedding to [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) and traveled to [Four Winds Harbor](../codex/places.md#four-winds-harbor) to visit the newlyweds, supporting [Anne](../character/anne.md) through both the tragic loss of her firstborn infant and the joyful birth of her son.

## Quotes

> "Well now, yes. It always kind of gives me a thrill to see them ugly white grubs that spade up in the cucumber beds. I hate the look of them."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER II. Matthew Cuthbert Is Surprised P58](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0058)

> "It’s five miles; and as you’re evidently bent on talking you might as well talk to some purpose by telling me what you know about yourself."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER V. Anne’s History P8](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0008)

> "No, I don’t want any of your imaginings. Just you stick to bald facts. Begin at the beginning. Where were you born and how old are you?"
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER V. Anne’s History P10](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0010)

> "We’re not talking about poetry, Anne—we are talking about saying your prayers. Don’t you know it’s a terrible wicked thing not to say your prayers every night? I’m afraid you are a very bad little girl."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER VII. Anne Says Her Prayers P11](../source/v01-c07.md#nw-v01-c07-p0011)

> "Well, you’ll have to do without your thrill. I hadn’t any material to waste on puffed sleeves. I think they are ridiculous-looking things anyhow. I prefer the plain, sensible ones."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER XI. Anne’s Impressions of Sunday-school P10](../source/v01-c11.md#nw-v01-c11-p0010)

## Relationships

### [Anne](../character/anne.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne--marilla-cuthbert.md)

Marilla took [Anne](../character/anne.md) in as an orphan, initially intending to return her after a mix-up at the orphanage. She soon took on the role of Anne's adoptive mother and guardian, establishing household rules and instructing her in practical tasks like cooking. Over time, Marilla's strict discipline gave way to deep affection, and she came to love [Anne](../character/anne.md) like a daughter.

- Commands — guardian ordering her to her room  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Properly Horrified P22](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0022), [v2 XII A Jonah Day P35](../source/v02-c12.md#nw-v02-c12-p0035)</sub>
